overview: Desktop Gomoku (15x15) with Tkinter UI and an AI opponent at three difficulty levels. MVC-style separation: game.py holds rules/state, ui.py renders and captures input without blocking, controller.py orchestrates turns and AI scheduling, ai.py computes moves (immediate block/win heuristics, center/adjacency bias), main.py wires everything and runs Tk event loop. AI runs on a background thread to keep UI responsive; controller ignores stale AI results via a job id. The view snaps clicks to nearest intersection within a radius, shows last move marker, winning line highlighting, turn/difficulty status, and provides New Game/Difficulty/Starter/Quit controls.

modules.name: main.py
modules.responsibility: Runnable entry point. Create Tk root, instantiate GomokuView and GameController, wire callbacks, start the Tk mainloop. Ensures clean shutdown on Quit.

modules.name: ui.py
modules.responsibility: Tkinter-based view: draw 15x15 board on a Canvas, snap clicks to intersections, display controls (New Game, Difficulty: Easy/Medium/Hard, Starter: Human/AI, Quit), show status/turn, last-move marker, and winning line highlighting. No blocking event loop inside; exposes callbacks to controller.
public_interfaces: class GomokuView:  def __init__(self, root: tkinter.Tk, board_size: int = 15, on_intersection_click: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None, on_new_game: Callable[[], None] | None = None, on_quit: Callable[[], None] | None = None, on_difficulty_change: Callable[[str], None] | None = None, on_starter_change: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> None
GomokuView.render_board(board: list[list[int]], last_move: tuple[int, int] | None = None, winning_line: list[tuple[int, int]] | None = None) -> None

modules.name: game.py
modules.responsibility: Core game model and rules. Maintains board state, turn management, move legality, win/draw detection, last move and winning line tracking. Provides a copy for AI evaluation.
public_interfaces: class GameState:  def __init__(self, board_size: int = 15, human_starts: bool = True) -> None
def check_winner(board: list[list[int]], row: int, col: int) -> tuple[int | None, list[tuple[int, int]] | None]

modules.name: ai.py
modules.responsibility: AI move selection. Provides a fast, deterministic-enough move picker per difficulty within time limits: Easy random/center-biased legal move; Medium/HARD block opponent immediate four-in-a-row with single gap; Hard also takes own immediate winning move when available; otherwise uses simple heuristics (adjacency/center bias). Pure compute function for use from a background thread.
public_interfaces: def compute_best_move(state: game.GameState, difficulty: str, time_limit: float) -> tuple[int, int]

modules.name: controller.py
modules.responsibility: Application controller. Wires view and game model, handles user input, enforces turn order, schedules AI on a background thread, applies difficulty and starter settings, manages game restarts and clean quit. Ensures UI responsiveness and ignores stale AI results via a job id.
public_interfaces: class GameController:  def __init__(self, root: tkinter.Tk, view: ui.GomokuView, default_difficulty: str = 'Medium', default_starter: str = 'Human') -> None

data_structures: Move: tuple[int, int] as (row, col), 0-based indices within [0, 14].

GameState fields: board_size:int; board:Board; next_color:int (1 or 2); human_color:int; ai_color:int; last_move:Optional[Move]; winning_line:Optional[list[Move]]; winner:Optional[int]; is_draw:bool; moves_count:int.
Starter: str in {'Human','AI'}; starter plays Black (color 1).
design_notes: Pattern: MVC. ui.py (View) is passive and callback-driven; game.py (Model) encapsulates rules; controller.py (Controller) coordinates input, model updates, view refresh, and AI scheduling.
UI: Tkinter Canvas draws grid, stones, last-move marker (e.g., ring or dot), and winning line highlight. Controls via Frame + ttk widgets; status via Label. No call to mainloop outside main.py.
Click handling: View snaps to nearest intersection within a pixel radius; if outside or occupied, no state change and a brief flash/status message is shown.
Turn/Rules: Controller checks GameState.is_legal before GameState.place_stone, toggles turn only on success, updates status, and checks for win/draw using game.check_winner and board_full.

AI: Background Thread per AI move to keep UI responsive. Controller deep-copies GameState (or Board) for AI. A monotonically increasing ai_job_id is used to discard late results after restarts or rapid inputs.

AI heuristics: Hard first searches for own immediate winning move, then blocks opponent win-in-one; Medium blocks opponent win-in-one; both otherwise prefer moves adjacent to last move or center-biased random among legal moves. Easy picks a quick center-biased random legal move. All paths are linear-time scans over empties (<=225), returning well within time caps.
Timing: Controller maps difficulty to time limits (Easy<=0.5s, Medium<=1.0s, Hard<=3.0s). AI compute function returns quickly; optional short sleep is avoided to keep UI snappy.

Responsiveness/Stability: No shared mutable state between UI thread and AI thread; only immutable copies passed to AI. All UI updates are marshaled to the Tk thread via root.after. New Game disables clicks until state reset; AI scheduling guarded to prevent double moves.

Accessibility: High-contrast stone colors with outlines; last-move marker and winning line use shape markers (e.g., ring and line) so information is not color-only; status text always indicates current turn and difficulty.
Portability: Standard library only (tkinter, threading, time, random); Python 3.10+ types (| unions).
